subject: Biology
description: Endocrine glands + hormones: pituitary, thyroid, pancreas, adrenal, gonads

questions.stem: MASTER GLAND of the human endocrine system is:
questions.explanation: PITUITARY = 'master gland' — pea-sized, attached to brain (below hypothalamus). Two parts: ANTERIOR (adenohypophysis) + POSTERIOR (neurohypophysis). SECRETES hormones that CONTROL other glands: GROWTH HORMONE (GH — stimulates growth; deficiency → dwarfism; excess → gigantism / acromegaly); TSH (Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone — controls thyroid); ACTH (controls adrenal cortex); FSH + LH (control gonads); PROLACTIN (milk production). POSTERIOR: ADH / vasopressin (water retention by kidneys); OXYTOCIN ('love hormone' — uterine contractions in labour, milk ejection, social bonding). HYPOTHALAMUS controls pituitary in turn (hypothalamic-pituitary axis). INSIGHT — pituitary is the conductor of endocrine 'orchestra'.

questions.stem: INSULIN is secreted by which gland?

options.option_text: Pancreas (beta cells of Islets of Langerhans)
Thyroid (in front of throat) too alone

questions.explanation: INSULIN — produced by BETA CELLS of ISLETS OF LANGERHANS in PANCREAS. LOWERS blood glucose (allows cells to absorb glucose). GLUCAGON (alpha cells) — opposite: raises blood glucose. DIABETES MELLITUS = problem with insulin: TYPE 1 (autoimmune destroys beta cells; need lifelong insulin shots; ~10%); TYPE 2 (insulin resistance OR impaired secretion; lifestyle-linked; ~90%). India has world's 2nd largest diabetes population (~80M; will be #1 soon). INSULIN HISTORY: discovered 1921 by BANTING + BEST + MACLEOD + COLLIP (Toronto, Canada); Nobel 1923. Pancreas also secretes digestive enzymes (exocrine — amylase, lipase, trypsin via duct to small intestine). Pancreas = both ENDOCRINE + EXOCRINE.

questions.explanation: THYROID — butterfly-shaped, in NECK, just below larynx (Adam's apple). Produces THYROXINE (T4) + TRIIODOTHYRONINE (T3) — regulate METABOLISM. Need IODINE for synthesis (~150 µg/day). DEFICIENCY: HYPOTHYROIDISM (low TH) → goitre (enlarged thyroid), weight gain, lethargy, cretinism (in children, retards mental + physical growth — preventable!). EXCESS: HYPERTHYROIDISM (Graves' disease) → weight loss, racing heart, anxiety, bulging eyes (exophthalmos). PREVENTION OF GOITRE: iodised salt (mandated by India 2005 — major public-health success). India's thyroid disorder rates ~10% of population, esp. women + Himalayan iodine-deficient regions. Also: CALCITONIN from thyroid (lowers blood calcium). PARATHYROID glands (4 small) on back of thyroid — secrete PTH (raises blood calcium).

questions.stem: ADRENALINE (epinephrine) is the 'fight-or-flight' hormone secreted by:
questions.explanation: ADRENALINE / EPINEPHRINE — from ADRENAL MEDULLA (inner adrenal gland; atop kidneys). FIGHT-OR-FLIGHT: increases HR + breathing rate, dilates pupils + airways, redirects blood from gut to muscles, releases glucose for energy, reduces digestion → all to prepare for emergency. Released during STRESS / FEAR. ADRENAL CORTEX (outer, separate from medulla) → CORTISOL (stress hormone, anti-inflammatory; medical: corticosteroids); ALDOSTERONE (regulates Na+/K+, blood pressure); SEX HORMONES (smaller amounts). MEDICAL: ADRENALINE injection used in: anaphylaxis (severe allergy — EpiPen), cardiac arrest, severe asthma. NOREPINEPHRINE — closely related, both neurotransmitter + hormone.

questions.stem: GROWTH HORMONE (GH) deficiency in childhood causes:
questions.explanation: Growth Hormone (GH / somatotropin) — anterior pituitary. Stimulates BONE + tissue growth. DEFICIENCY in childhood → DWARFISM (proportional short stature; can be treated with GH injections). EXCESS in childhood → GIGANTISM (very tall — over 7-8 ft; e.g., basketball players have a touch of this, sometimes pathologically). EXCESS in adulthood (after growth plates close) → ACROMEGALY (bones thicken; jaw, hands, feet enlarge; abnormal facial features — e.g., Andre the Giant). Both gigantism + acromegaly often from pituitary tumour. India: famous case of dwarf actors like KISAN BAHUGUNA, AHSAAN QURESHI and others. THYROID issues in children (deficiency) → CRETINISM (different from dwarfism; affects brain too).

questions.stem: MELATONIN, the 'sleep hormone', is secreted by:
questions.explanation: MELATONIN — secreted by PINEAL GLAND (tiny pinecone-shaped gland in brain). Released in DARKNESS (nighttime); LIGHT (esp. blue) suppresses it. Regulates SLEEP-WAKE CYCLE (circadian rhythm). Why night-time SCREEN USE disturbs sleep: blue light from phones suppresses melatonin → harder to fall asleep. JET LAG = melatonin cycle out of sync with new time zone (resolves over days). MELATONIN supplements (over-the-counter) used for jet lag, insomnia. DESCARTES called pineal the 'seat of the soul' (philosophical, now disputed). Aging → less melatonin → older people often have poorer sleep. INSIGHT — pineal also has photoreceptive function (active in some non-mammalian vertebrates as 'third eye'); in mammals, vestigial. Lights-out before bed for better sleep!

questions.stem: TESTOSTERONE (male sex hormone) is mainly produced by:
questions.explanation: TESTOSTERONE — primary male sex hormone; produced by LEYDIG cells in TESTES. Functions: development of male SECONDARY SEXUAL CHARACTERISTICS (deeper voice, facial/body hair, muscle mass, sperm production, libido). Adrenal glands also secrete small amounts (in both sexes). FEMALE EQUIVALENT: ESTROGEN + PROGESTERONE (from ovaries, adrenal smaller amount). PUBERTY = surge in sex hormones (ages 9-14 girls, 11-15 boys). PITUITARY hormones LH + FSH stimulate gonads to produce sex hormones (HPG axis = hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal). ANDROGEN — class of male hormones (testosterone is one). TESTOSTERONE in females (small amounts) — affects libido + muscle. DOPING in sports often involves anabolic steroids = synthetic testosterone analogs.
